name: Graphene
equilibrium_context: Two-dimensional Dirac semimetal, topologically trivial, time-reversal symmetric; epitaxially on SiC a substrate-induced gap at the Dirac point of about 0.27 eV
summary: The prototype since Oka and Aoki 2009 and the sharpest point of contention: the Floquet BANDS have been spectroscopically established since 2025/2026, the attribution of the TRANSPORT signal to their topology is open.

driven_states.emergent_property: First-order Floquet-Bloch sidebands of the Dirac cone. No hybridization gap resolved: calculated 70 and 21 meV respectively, both below the respective energy resolution of 155 and 53 meV. Significance: Floquet engineering is possible at all in a semimetal with decoherence times of a few tens of femtoseconds.

drive.polarization: linear, angle tuned to nearly s

driven_states.source: Merboldt et al., Nature Physics 21, 1093 (2025), doi:10.1038/s41567-025-02889-7
driven_states.caveat: Two independent groups, back to back in the same issue - but no demonstration of a gap; the actual topological effect remains unproven in both works. The distinction from Volkov states is made not by omission but via the momentum asymmetry of the sideband as a fingerprint of quantum-path interference - methodologically weaker than a null test and dependent on the quality of the simulation.

threshold.quantity: none - Floquet dressing has no threshold

further_sources: Choi, Mogi, De Giovannini et al., Nature Physics 21, 1100 (2025), doi:10.1038/s41567-025-02888-8 (independent group)
driven_states.measured_quantity: time- and angle-resolved photoemission, sideband intensity and asymmetry

driven_states.emergent_property: Light-induced hybridization gap at the Floquet band crossings: 241 +/- 18 meV at 490 meV photon energy and 4.1 mJ/cm^2, accompanied by coherent sidebands. Pronounced momentum anisotropy - the gap vanishes along the light polarization and is maximal perpendicular to it; two Dirac nodes protected by space-time symmetry remain, and their position can be steered by polarization.
driven_states.source: Wang, Cai, Tang et al., Nature Materials 25, 1140 (2026), doi:10.1038/s41563-026-02549-y
driven_states.caveat: The turning point of the field: for the first time a gap that one sees rather than infers by calculation - ratio of gap to resolution 3.4 versus 0.45 and 0.40 in the 2025 works. However: only one group (Tsinghua), the gap extraction hinges on multi-peak fits whose result depends on the momentum integration window, and the Floquet parameter already lies outside the clear weak-field regime. The Floquet Chern insulator is therefore NOT demonstrated: at linear polarization the gap is not topological.

threshold.quantity: none - the gap grows continuously with the field

driven_states.measured_quantity: angle-resolved photoemission, hybridization gap at the avoided crossing

driven_states.emergent_property: Transverse Hall conductance without magnetic field, sign follows the helicity; plateau at 1.8 +/- 0.4 e^2/h for Fermi energies below about 30 meV, plateau width about 60 meV, close to the calculated Floquet gap of 69 meV.
driven_states.source: McIver, Schulte, Stein, Matsuyama, Jotzu, Meier & Cavalleri, Nature Physics 16, 38 (2020), doi:10.1038/s41567-019-0698-y
driven_states.caveat: The topological interpretation is NOT secure. Three independent points of criticism: first, the bulk of the signal, even in the authors' own modeling, stems from a population asymmetry rather than from a Berry-curvature anomalous velocity; second, an independent experiment (Candussio) produces a qualitatively similar circular Hall effect purely kinetically and thermally; third, helicity-dependent photoresistance measurements are demonstrably susceptible to thermal gradients induced by beam displacement. All transport data come from one group; an independent replication is not known.
further_sources: Sato et al., Phys. Rev. B 99, 214302 (2019), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.99.214302 (Berry contribution small)
Candussio et al., Phys. Rev. B 105, 155416 (2022), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.105.155416 (thermal-kinetic alternative)
Murotani et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 131, 096901 (2023), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.131.096901
Yang et al., Nat. Commun. 13 (2022), doi:10.1038/s41467-022-34198-5 (beam-displacement artifacts)
driven_states.measured_quantity: Hall conductance in e^2/h, on-chip THz transport via photoconductive switch

driven_states.emergent_property: Helicity-dependent transverse photoconductivity without magnetic field, with sign reversal; linear in intensity at low gate voltages, quadratic at high ones.
driven_states.source: Candussio et al., Phys. Rev. B 105, 155416 (2022), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.105.155416
driven_states.caveat: Deliberately listed as a separate entry because it carries the thermal-kinetic counter-position with its own data: the authors attribute the signal to momentum alignment by the combined THz and static field as well as to dynamic heating and cooling of the electron gas - no Floquet topology, no Berry curvature. Note: a different regime, field about forty times smaller and pulse duration five orders of magnitude longer than in McIver. The entry does not refute McIver directly, but it shows that a helicity-dependent Hall effect arises without any topological ingredient.
driven_states.measured_quantity: transverse photovoltage as a function of backgate and intensity

sources: Merboldt et al., Nature Physics 21, 1093 (2025), doi:10.1038/s41567-025-02889-7
Wang et al., Nature Materials 25, 1140 (2026), doi:10.1038/s41563-026-02549-y
McIver et al., Nature Physics 16, 38 (2020), doi:10.1038/s41567-019-0698-y
Candussio et al., Phys. Rev. B 105, 155416 (2022), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.105.155416
gaps: The Floquet bands demonstrably exist; whether the 2020 transport signal is to be attributed to their topology is open, and the evidence leans rather in the opposite direction.
No independent replication of the transport experiment as of August 2026.
